articles.title: B/R Staff Predictions for UFC 333 Main Card
articles.summary: UFC 333 is right around the corner, and it is one of the deepest cards of the year on paper, with elite talent from the bottom of the bill to the top.
articles.body:
UFC 333 is right around the corner, and it is one of the deepest cards of the year on paper, with elite talent from the bottom of the bill to the top.

The main event will see featherweight legend Alexander Volkanovski attempt to defend his belt against Movsar Evloev, who has yet to be beaten in 20 professional fights.

There will also be a title up for grabs in the co-main event, as bantamweight champ Petr Yan takes on challenger Merab Dvalishvili. It will be the third time the two bantamweight greats have met in the Octagon, after splitting their first two meetings 1-1.

The remainder of the main card will be packed with exciting contenders. That includes a flyweight fight between top-10 talents Lone'er Kavanagh and Ramazan Temirov, a heavyweight showdown between hulking Russians Alexander Volkov and Rizvan Kuniev, and a featherweight scrap between proven finishers Losene Keita and Aaron Pico.

It has the makings of a very exciting night of MMA.

Here's how the B/R combat sports team sees it all going down.

Adam Kramer: The oddsmakers essentially see this as a coin flip , which feels about right. And given their contrasting styles, this feels like one of the more unique MMA chess matches in recent memory.

That said, we know what each fighter would like to do. Volkanovski wants to strike, and he wants to rely on incredible footwork and technique to do so. Evloev wants to clinch, wrestle, and ultimately bring the fight to the ground.

Thus far, that style has worked for the challenger. He's 20-0, after all. It's not the sexiest way to win, but Evloev is a real threat, and he's showcased that against an incredible lineup of fighters over his past five fights.

Volkanovski recovered nicely after back-to-back losses with two wins, albeit both coming over Diego Lopes. Still, he's 38 years old and likely to be pushed at a frantic pace unless he can end this fight early.

This one doesn't have to be all that complicated. If they stay standing, Volk wins. If Evloev makes it ugly, he likely does enough to win by decision. I believe he'll do that, even if Volkanovski threatens throughout. What a fun matchup.

Prediction: Evloev by unanimous decision

Tom Taylor: Movsar Evloev's record is pretty darn shiny, but I suspect it will be tarnished at the hands of Alexander Volkanovski this weekend.

The champ himself has given a pretty good assessment of this matchup, I think. He believes the only way Evloev beats him is by catching him somehow, and given that the challenger has not scored a finish in 10 straight fights—on the feet or on the mat—it's very hard to see that happening.

Yes, Evloev has the wrestling and cardio to potentially win a decision, but Volkanovski was able to hang with Islam Makhachev in the grappling, and Makhachev, who is now the welterweight champ, is way bigger and way better than Evloev.

Long story short, Evloev is unlikely to show Volkanovski anything he hasn't seen before, and he doesn't have the firepower or killer instinct to surprise the champ. Volkanovski sets the terms of the fight and wins a clear decision.

Prediction: Volkanovski by unanimous decision

Lyle Fitzsimmons: If you're a UFC fan, you're probably an Alex fan. In fact, I was driving in my car yesterday, heard "Down Under" on the radio, and immediately thought of the last time I was in a building for one of his ring walks. Quite the spectacle.

Volkanovski reinvented himself – thanks to Diego Lopes – after he was splattered by Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria, but at 38 years old and with another hungry lion charging, can he keep the Aussie mojo going?

The guess here is no. I don't foresee a pretty fight or a particularly fan-friendly one. But Evloev has shown he can get top-end guys down and keep them there. That's not great news for the fans. And it'd be even worse news for Volkanovski.

Adam Kramer: Why should this fight go different than the one we saw back in December? It's a fair place to begin.

As shocking as it was, the formula to stop Dvalishvili wasn't all that complicated. Yan's takedown defense was superb in that fight, and he seemed to break his opponent even more as the night went on.

Still, Merab fought four times last year. In his fight against Yan, it showed. And for the first time in a long time, he looked gassed.

A long layoff was needed for Merab, and it should do him extraordinarily well. How he changes his game plan will be fascinating to watch, as will Yan's adjustments following such a dominant win last time they fought.

Merab, now a decent-sized underdog, will be better conditioned. And the attempts to bring this down to the mat should be different this time around. Maybe doubting Yan given everything we saw between these two less than a year ago will be a mistake, but it's one we're willing to try.

A rested Merab will prove to be a much more functional Merab.

Tom Taylor: I was very confident Merab Dvalishvili would beat Petr Yan last time they fought. I was very wrong about that, and I won't make the same mistake again.

While I consider Dvalishvili the best bantamweight of all time, Yan really seemed to figure him out last time—figure him out in a way that will be difficult to undo. He stopped takedowns, weathered Dvalishvili's non-stop aggression, and fired back with heavy artillery from bell to bell. I see no reason why he won't be able to do something similar again.

I agree that Dvalishvili will probably be well rested and better prepared this time around, but I really don't see what changes he can implement to beat the Yan that showed up when they last met.

I'm calling for a repeat of the second fight. It'll be reasonably close, but Yan will once again get the win after five fun rounds.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Simple question. From which fight do you pull the most evidence?

The first one, when a pre-reign Dvalishvili scored 11 takedowns and nearly seven minutes of control time? Or the second, in which he was denied on all but two of his takedown tries while Yan mixed his own striking attack to the head, body, and legs?

Prediction: Dvalishvili by unanimous decision

Adam Kramer: The Kavanagh hype was upended back in July against Brandon Royval, and there's no shame in that. Royval has done that to others before and remains a matchup nightmare regardless of the opponent.

In terms of style, Temirov will be much different. Kavanagh's biggest worry here, first and foremost, should be power rather than submission. Temirov has ended four of his last five fights in the first round and two of those wins came in the first 60 seconds.

That could be an issue for Kavanagh, who has been finished in two of his last three fights.

Granted, he's a superb fighter with a significant reach advantage. Taking advantage of that reach will be critical, as it will allow him to avoid trouble.

The problem is that the power difference is enormous. And in terms of the fight outcome, it just feels like that could ultimately be the deciding factor.

Tom Taylor: This is a really hard fight to call, and it's almost impossible to feel confident about the outcome either way.

That said, I'm going to go with Lone'er Kavanagh. There's definitely a huge risk he'll be finished by Ramazan Temirov, who is both extremely aggressive and absurdly powerful for the flyweight division, but I think he is smart enough to be cautious and use his range and cardio to control the action after his opponent's initial assault.

He may never be champ, but I don't place too much stock in his loss to Brandon Royval. He's still clearly very good. Good enough, I believe, to win this fight on points.

Prediction: Kavanagh by unanimous decision

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Who imposes his will, or at least his fighting style, on the other guy?

Can Kavanagh bounce back from two losses in his last three fights – both inside the distance – or are the losses to Charles Johnson and Brandon Royval indications that he doesn't belong at the highest level?

Temirov is certainly a challenge, given that he beat Johnson and blew away former title challenger Steve Erceg, and it says here that it's too much for Kavanagh to handle.

Adam Kramer: Let's start with the height and reach advantages, which are pretty much where every fight featuring Volkov should start. At 6'7", he'll be three inches taller and have a four-inch reach advantage over Kuniev, who will do everything possible to close the distance and make this fight ugly.

It's the right plan, although Volkov could very well be up for it. In fact, it's remarkable how good he has been over his last five fights, which include four wins and one split-decision loss against Ciryl Gane.

He's fought grapplers, he's fought balanced fighters, and he's fought heavy-handed fighters like Sergei Pavlovich. Volkov's measurements and style have proven to be a challenge for just about everyone, and it feels like that will be the case once again.

Kuniev will do his best to break the rhythm, but it won't be enough.

Prediction: Volkov by unanimous decision

Tom Taylor: Outside of Tom Aspinall, whose future in the sport is very uncertain at the moment, there is no heavyweight in the UFC I'd pick to beat Volkov right now. Years after his brief reign as Bellator heavyweight champ, and after some serious inconsistency, the towering Russian has seemingly found his groove. He's beaten everyone the UFC has put in front of him in recent years, with the exception of an absolute robbery against Ciryl Gane. I can't see that changing on Saturday. Rizvan Kuniev has looked decent in the UFC, scraping by Jailton Almeida and knocking out Tyrell Fortune in his two Octagon wins, but neither of those performances was particularly mind-blowing, and neither opponent is anywhere near Volkov's level.

Volkov's experience at the highest level will carry him to victory in this one. Kuniev is unlikely to give him any new looks, which will allow him to use his range to cruise to a wide decision—maybe even a late stoppage.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Every time I play the "yeah, sure, Volkov is tall, but (opponent name goes here) can do this, this, and this to him in spite of the size differential." And then I'm wrong.

It's been that way for five years, beyond losses to guys named Ciryl Gane and Tom Aspinall.

I appreciate how good Kuniev is and how he's only lost (by a narrow decision) once in the last 10 years. But I'm not getting fooled again. At least not the way I have been.

Adam Kramer: The whole notion that "styles make fights" might be tiring to some, although it feels appropriate here. And there's something beautiful in MMA when two fighters find enormous success through two very different routes.

For Keita, he wants to be upright. He wants to strike. He wants to end this fight early, which he has done 11 of his 17 wins. If this doesn't go to the mat, Keita has an enormous advantage.

For Pico, who will be fighting in his third UFC fight after an impressive Bellator run, wrestling will certainly be part of his strategy.

He has heavy hands, and he will use them at times. Although his strong wrestling background coupled with his opponent should make the strategy somewhat simplified here. And that wrestling and grappling should be put to use early and often.

Pico will pick his spots, avoid the big shot and that will be enough.

Tom Taylor: At his best, Aaron Pico is one of the most technically proficient and naturally gifted fighters I've ever seen. His recent win over Patricio "Pitbull" Freire was evidence of this. He looked incredible in the Octagon that night. Near perfect.

That said, I really don't like this matchup for him. On paper, he has all the tools to win—namely his elite wrestling, which we don't often see in his fights. Unfortunately, he is prone to throwing caution to the wind, which almost never works out for him, because he is one of the least durable fighters in the sport. Against a knockout artist like Keita, that could be a huge problem.

This is such a weird matchup, because if Pico fights to his potential, he should win very easily, but it's just hard to trust him to do that.

I see him starting strong, slipping into autopilot, and walking into something that puts him out. I don't want it to happen that way, but I have a feeling that's how it will go down.

Lyle Fitzsimmons: Pico is one of what seems like a bunch of recent guys who did great things at Bellator only to arrive at the UFC and fall immediately short.

His fight with Patricio Pitbull in April was a showdown of two of those guys, in fact.

But there's still a lot to like with Pico, particularly given his not-so-advanced age (30) and what seems like a favorable style matchup here.

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez's super-middleweight world title fight with Christian Mbilli still set to go on in Riyadh despite conflict
articles.summary: Canelo Alvarez's fight with Christian Mbilli for the WBC title is still set to go ahead in Riyadh on October 31; Riyadh's airport was bombed earlier this month and other sports events in Riyadh have been postponed; But Mbilli's promoter said: "I'm very confident the fight goes ahead"
articles.body:
Riyadh's King Khalid airport has been bombed in recent days during the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

The UK government is warning against non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia, the US advises citizens to reconsider travel there.

Despite those risks the show currently looks set to go ahead.

Mbilli isn't backing down. His promoter Camille Estephan told Sky Sports : "Christian will arrive in Saudi as planned.

"I'm very confident the fight goes ahead and Mbilli will keep his belt and dethrone Canelo, God willing."

It's a significant fight for Canelo. It will be his first bout since Terence Crawford defeated him in a spectacular performance in 2025.

When Crawford retired the super-middleweight titles scattered.

Canada's Mbilli is undefeated, winning the WBC interim 168lb belt when he beat Maciej Sulecki. He retained the strap when he drew with Lester Martinez last year. He was then upgraded to full world championship status when Crawford vacated the title.

Mexican superstar Canelo, looking to come back with a win and reclaim his old title, has boxed in Riyadh once before, a unanimous points win over William Scull.

Other sports events, like tennis' Six Kings Slam, that were due to take place in Riyadh have been postponed.

articles.title: Mayweather quiere encontrar al único boxeador que le venció para ayudarlo: “Está sin hogar”
articles.standfirst: 'Money' habla en PBD Podcast de una posible revancha con McGregor, de los más de 500 millones que le han estafado y de un antiguo y desaparecido rival
articles.summary: 'Money' habla en PBD Podcast de una posible revancha con McGregor, de los más de 500 millones que le han estafado y de un antiguo y desaparecido rival
articles.body: Floyd Mayweather ha intervenido en PBD Podcast de Youtube y allí ha hablado de diferentes temas, como su posible revancha con Conor McGregor o su situación financiera. Ha reconocido que gran parte de su fortuna se esfumó, pues personas en las que confiaba le robaron más de 500 millones de dólares. "Un hombre que era algo así como una figura paterna para mí me robó 350 millones de dólares. Me estaba ayudando y yo creía que era mi amigo. Años después empezamos a revisar la documentación y descubrimos que había desaparecido el dinero", ha confesado Floyd. Esta no fue la única supuesta estafa que sufrió ‘Pretty Boy’ según ha explicado: “Había un hombre que se hacía pasar por mi amigo, que me ayudaba a poner en orden mis negocios y me robó 200 millones de dólares más". El expúgil, sin embargo, admite: “Nací pobre, puedo caer hasta el fondo, pero puedo volver a la cima. Sé cómo escalar, la mierda pasa. Sigo viviendo muy bien". Actualmente el excampeón está en litigios con Al Haymon y Stephen Espinoza, dos de los hombres clave en la vida financiera de Mayweather. Sea como fuere, ‘Money’ mantiene su interés en organizar peleas de exhibición para ganar dinero y el nombre de Conor McGregor salió a colación: “Creo que Conor McGregor y yo podríamos volver a pelear. Sí, absolutamente. No vivo con Conor McGregor, no es mi amigo, no tengo que verlo. Simplemente, cuando llegue el momento de hacer negocios y pelear, hagámoslo". Hay un nombre que quizás nadie esperaba y del que también se habló: Serafim Todorov, el último boxeador que venció a Mayweather, concretamente en las semifinales de los Juegos Olímpicos de Atlanta en 1996. "En realidad, el tipo con el que perdí, creo que ahora está sin hogar, por lo que me han dicho. Todo pasa por una razón, pero no le deseo el mal a nadie. Si puedo encontrarlo y darle dinero o prestarle ayuda, no hay problema", dijo el expúgil de 49 años. El presentador de PBD Podcast (Patrick Bet-David), preguntó: "¿Lo harías?" A lo que Floyd respondió: “Absolutamente”; PBD replicó: “¿Qué tal si me dejas ir a buscarlo? Lo voy a encontrar”. Lanzado el guante, cabe recordar que el búlgaro Serafim Todorov (57 años) fue tres veces campeón del mundo amateur, pero desde que ganó aquella medalla de plata en Atlanta su carrera y su vida ya fueron cuesta abajo. Intentó competir en los Juegos de Sídney bajo nacionalidad turca, que le pagaba un buen dinero por representarlos, pero esa idea naufragó. Se acabó haciendo profesional y tuvo una carrera corta e intrascendente. Dejó el pugilismo y comenzó a trabajar en cualquier cosa que le salía. Tuvo problemas con el alcohol y aseguró que le ofrecieron trabajo en el crimen organizado, camino que rechazó. Lo último que se supo de él, hace ya más de una década, es que vivía con una ayuda estatal de menos de 500 euros al mes para él y su familia.

articles.title: Manny Pacquiao Fight on Tyson Fury-Joshua Card Agreed to by Joe Cordina, Latest Details Revealed
articles.summary: It sounds like boxing legend Manny Pacquiao could be in action later this year.
articles.body:
It sounds like boxing legend Manny Pacquiao could be in action later this year.

Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn told BoxingScene.com that Joe Cordina has "agreed terms to face Pacquiao, but we don't know if it's happening. From our side, we've agreed to do it." The fight would take place on the Dec. 11 Netflix card headlined by heavyweight legends Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

A two-time IBF super-featherweight champion, Cordina would be in the biggest fight of his career if Pacquiao agrees to terms. The 19-1 slugger most recently fought in December, earning a unanimous decision win over Gabriel Flores Jr. in his second appearance since moving back up to lightweight.

At 47 years old, Pacquiao is still one of the biggest names in boxing. He returned to the ring after a four-year hiatus in July 2025, fighting WBC welterweight champion Mario Barrios to a draw. His impressive performance fueled optimism that he could continue his boxing career despite his age.

Earlier this year, it was announced that Pacquiao would face Floyd Mayweather Jr. in a rematch of their iconic 2015 clash. However, the fight was postponed indefinitely after Mayweather was sued for breach of contract.

While there would be a significant age difference against the 34-year-old Cordina, the allure of being on the biggest boxing card of the year could be tough for Pacquiao to turn down. Fury and Joshua have been building towards their showdown for over a decade, so their main event would certainly draw a large audience.

Adding Pacquiao to the card would boost the fan interest even further, so many will be keeping their fingers crossed that he agrees to face Cordina.

articles.title: Who is Alexander Volkov? Meet the UFC heavyweight contender known as Drago who is set to fight at UFC 333
articles.summary: Alexander Volkov is a Russian mixed martial artist who competes in the UFC heavyweight division.
articles.body: Alexander Volkov is a Russian mixed martial artist who competes in the UFC heavyweight division. Known by his nickname “Drago,” he has established himself as one of the division’s most experienced fighters. He is a former heavyweight champion in both Bellator MMA and M-1 Global.Standing 6 feet 7 inches tall, Volkov is known for his powerful striking, technical boxing and impressive reach. He has earned major victories over former champions and top contenders, including Fabricio Werdum, Alistair Overeem and Sergei Pavlovich. As of now, he is ranked No. 4 in the Meta UFC heavyweight rankings.Who is Alexander Volkov?Alexander Yevgenyevich Volkov was born on October 24, 1988, in Moscow, Russia. He began his professional MMA career in April 2009. He soon developed a reputation as a dangerous heavyweight. He won his first two fights by technical knockout before suffering his first professional defeat by submission.Volkov continued improving and competed in several promotions before reaching international prominence. In 2012, he joined Bellator MMA and entered its heavyweight tournament. He defeated Brett Rogers and Vinicius Queiroz before beating Richard Hale by unanimous decision to win the Bellator Heavyweight Championship in December 2012.His first title reign ended in November 2013 when Vitaly Minakov stopped him in the first round. Volkov bounced back by winning the Bellator Season 10 heavyweight tournament in 2014. However, consecutive losses to Tony Johnson and Cheick Kongo in 2015 led to his departure from the promotion.Volkov later returned to M-1 Global and captured its heavyweight championship in February 2016. He defended the title successfully against former Bellator light heavyweight champion Attila Vegh later that year.The Russian fighter signed with the UFC in September 2016. He made his promotional debut against Timothy Johnson in November, winning by split decision. He then defeated Roy Nelson and Stefan Struve before producing one of the biggest victories of his career.In March 2018, Volkov knocked out former UFC heavyweight champion Fabricio Werdum in the fourth round. The performance earned him a Performance of the Night bonus and strengthened his position among the division’s leading contenders.In 2023, Volkov submitted Tai Tuivasa with an Ezekiel choke, becoming only the second fighter in UFC history to finish a fight using that technique. He also defeated Sergei Pavlovich by unanimous decision in June 2024.Volkov narrowly lost a controversial split decision to Ciryl Gane in December 2024. He returned to winning ways against Jailton Almeida in October 2025 and Waldo Cortes-Acosta in May 2026.With 40 wins and 11 losses in 51 professional fights, Volkov has recorded 24 knockout victories, four submission wins and 12 decision victories. articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Joe Cordina agrees terms to face great Manny Pacquiao in Cardiff
articles.summary: Promoter Eddie Hearn says former world champion Joe Cordina has agreed terms to face boxing great Manny Pacquiao on the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua undercard.
articles.body:
Boxing great Manny Pacquiao, 47, could be added to the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua undercard - with former world champion Joe Cordina having agreed terms as his opponent.

Fury and Joshua are set to meet in an all-British heavyweight battle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.

Now promoter Eddie Hearn has confirmed that negotiations for a mouth-watering fight on the undercard are at an advanced stage.

"We've agreed terms to face Pacquiao, but we don't know if it's happening," Hearn revealed at a media event on Thursday.

Tickets for Fury-Joshua sold out in just one hour, and fight fans could now also be able to see iconic eight-weight world champion Pacquiao face Wales' former super-featherweight world champion Cordina.

Pacquiao is regarded as one of the best boxers of all time, and it would be the first time the 12-time former champion has fought in the UK.

Details of other fights on the eagerly anticipated clash are yet to be released.

The compromises and power struggles that shaped Fury-Joshua

Ex-boxing world champion Joe Cordina cleared of assault after petrol station punch

Pacquiao has not fought since July 2025, having returned from his second attempt at retirement.

But the Filipino icon would still be a draw for the huge television audience expected for the fight, that will be broadcast globally by streaming giants Netflix.

But the emergence of Cardiff-born Cordina, 34, as an opponent will also provide a hometown flavour to the show.

A former IBF super-featherweight champion, Cordina had been scheduled to face American Abduallah Mason for the WBO lightweight title in Cleveland in July when he was denied a US visa.

Cordina had remained in training while standing trial for allegations of assault, eventually being cleared of all charges .

That verdict has paved the way for a place on the Joshua-Fury bill, with Cordina eager to resume his career on what would be a huge opportunity in his own city.

It would be the first time Pacquiao has faced a British opponent since he beat Ricky Hatton in Las Vegas in 2009.

Pacquiao's last fight was a failed bid to take Mario Barrios' welterweight title, the bout ending in a majority draw four years after retiring to focus on politics in is homeland.

He has a record of 62 wins from 73 fights and had been scheduled to face unbeaten Floyd Mayweather in September, but the rematch of their 2015 meeting was postponed indefinitely in June.

Cordina has previously fought on the undercard of Fury's first fight with Oleksandr Usyk, losing his IBF title to Belfast's Anthony Cacace in Riyadh in May 2024.

It would represent the former Olympian's first fight in Cardiff since he regained the belt against Shavkat Rahimov the previous year.

articles.title: David Benavidez, Vergil Ortiz Jr. championship doubleheader official for December
articles.summary: Benavidez, the unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion, will fight Polish WBC titlist Michal Cieslak on Dec. 5. And in the co-feature, Ortiz will end a 13...
articles.body:
Two of boxing's most exciting fighters, David Benavidez and Vergil Ortiz Jr., will be sharing the stage later this year.

Benavidez, the unified WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion, will fight Polish WBC titlist Michal Cieslak on Dec. 5 at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona. And in the co-feature, Ortiz will end a 13-month layoff against former champion Keith Thurman.

The pay-per-view doubleheader will be available on DAZN and Amazon Prime Video, and it will also be part of the DAZN Ultimate subscription.

Benavidez (32-0, 26 KOs), a three-division world champion, surged through the pound-for-pound rankings in May after his impressive sixth-round destruction of Gilberto "Zurdo" Ramirez.

Cieslak (28-2, 22 KOs) captured the WBC interim title by stopping Jean Pascal in June 2025. He hasn't fought since, but he received the biggest news of his career when he was upgraded to full champion in September after Noel Mikaelian's title was stripped.

Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs) is the WBC interim super welterweight champion, but his Dec. 12 fight with Thurman will be contested at the middleweight limit — and it is expected Ortiz will continue his career at 160 pounds.

Ortiz was last in action when he knocked out Erickson Lubin in two rounds last November. He was in negotiations to face Jaron "Boots" Ennis in one of boxing's most anticipated fights, but Ortiz found himself tangled in a legal battle with his promoter, Oscar De La Hoya's Golden Boy, instead.

Ortiz and Golden Boy ultimately settled and agreed to complete the three fights remaining on their promotional deal beginning in December.

Thurman (31-2, 23 KOs), a former unified welterweight champion, is looking to bounce back from his one-sided KO defeat to WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian Fundora in March. Thurman, 37, has been inactive in the last few years and has not recorded a significant win since his unanimous decision victory over Mario Barrios in February 2022. He will be a heavy underdog against Ortiz.

articles.title: Eddie Alvarez net worth 2026: How the Underground King built his fortune across MMA, his UFC career, wins and more
articles.summary: Eddie Alvarez is one of the most accomplished lightweight fighters of his generation.
articles.body: Eddie Alvarez is one of the most accomplished lightweight fighters of his generation. Known as “The Underground King,” he became a champion in Bellator and the UFC during a career that spanned more than two decades.Alvarez built his reputation through high-level fights against some of MMA’s biggest names. He defeated Michael Chandler, Shinya Aoki, Anthony Pettis, Rafael dos Anjos and Justin Gaethje. He later moved into bare-knuckle boxing and continued competing at a high level.What is Eddie Alvarez’ net worth in 2026As of 2026, Eddie Alvarez has an estimated net worth of $8 million (per celebrity net worth). His wealth has come from his long MMA career, championship fights, bonuses, sponsorships and major contracts outside the UFC.Alvarez became Bellator’s first Lightweight Champion in 2009. He later regained the title after losing it to Michael Chandler in their famous 2011 fight. Their 2013 rematch ended with Alvarez winning by split decision.His biggest career breakthrough came after joining the UFC in 2014. Alvarez defeated Gilbert Melendez and Anthony Pettis before facing Rafael dos Anjos for the UFC Lightweight Championship in July 2016.Alvarez stopped dos Anjos in the first round to become UFC champion. He became the first fighter to win both the Bellator and UFC lightweight titles.His reign lasted only four months. At UFC 205, Alvarez faced Conor McGregor at Madison Square Garden. McGregor stopped him in the second round and became the first simultaneous two-division UFC champion.Alvarez still earned significant money during his UFC career. His disclosed purse for his UFC debut against Donald Cerrone was $100,000. He received another $100,000 for his win over Pettis and $150,000 for defeating dos Anjos. He also received a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus for the championship victory.After leaving the UFC in 2018, Alvarez signed with ONE Championship. He described the agreement as a guaranteed eight-figure package. That meant the deal was worth at least $10 million, although the exact amount he eventually received was never disclosed.His ONE Championship run produced one win, two losses and one no contest. He later moved to Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship.Alvarez defeated former UFC title challenger Chad Mendes by split decision in his BKFC debut in 2023. He then lost to Mike Perry before facing Jeremy Stephens in Philadelphia in 2025.Alvarez finished his professional MMA career with a record of 30 wins, eight losses and two no contests. His résumé includes victories over several former champions and elite contenders.Eddie Alvarez’ personal life His success also transformed his personal life. Alvarez grew up in Philadelphia’s Kensington neighborhood and began boxing at a young age. Before MMA became financially successful, he worked construction while supporting his family.He and his wife, Jamie, have four children. articles.title: Watch Arman Tsarukyan, Dillon Danis Brawl in Chaotic Video Ahead of RAF 14 Fight
articles.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Dillon Danis were involved in a brawl ahead of their freestyle wrestling match at RAF 14 in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Arman Tsarukyan and Dillon Danis were involved in a brawl ahead of their freestyle wrestling match at RAF 14 in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Filip Hrgovic on course for title defence against Frank Sanchez in Croatia before a unification with Daniel Dubois
articles.summary: IBF heavyweight world champion Filip Hrgovic looks to be on course for a mandatory title defence against Frank Sanchez next; He's likely to have a homecoming bout in Croatia next against Sanchez; Hrgovic's hopes of an immediate unification with WBO champ Daniel Dubois are on hold
articles.body:
Hrgovic won the IBF heavyweight world championship when he scored an upset stoppage win over Moses Itauma in August.

He was ringside on Saturday at The O2 arena to watch Daniel Dubois defend his WBO heavyweight championship and even faced off with the Londoner.

But rather than an immediate unification with Dubois, Hrgovic looks set to make a mandatory IBF title defence against Frank Sanchez in Croatia.

Sanchez's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports : "I expect Frank Sanchez versus Filip Hrgovic to take place in the first quarter of 2027, perhaps in Zagreb, but too early to know for sure."

He continued: "I have already communicated with George Warren [of Queensberry promotions] and will likely speak again this week. Frank has speed and power, but also brings experience and stamina, so he is anxious to fight Hrgovic.

"[Sanchez's trainer] Eddie Reynoso loves the match and so do I. Sanchez will become the first Cuban heavyweight champion."

Zagreb is a potential location for the Hrgovic-Sanchez fight and the local arena has welcomed the possibility.

Sretan Saric, the manager director of Arena Zagreb, told Sky Sports : "Of course I support the opportunity to hold the fight at Arena Zagreb."

Dubois has previously beaten Hrgovic but will be open to boxing the Croatian once again.

"To win all the belts. That's the main thing now for me, collecting all the other belts," he previously told Sky Sports .

"It would mean everything to have all those belts. No one can take that away from me. That's what I'm after now.

"Any one of them, Hrgovic, he was there on Saturday, maybe him or [WBC champion Agit] Kabayel," he said. "Hrgovic was tough as well, Kabayel, we'll see, we'll see what he's about. He ain't been in with a guy like me but he's a good fighter.

"Just anyone with a damn belt… Anyone who wants it."

articles.title: With Brandon Royval setback behind him, Lone’er Kavanagh braces for Ramazan Temirov’s knockout threat at UFC 333
articles.summary: Lone’er Kavanagh has not made major changes to his preparation for Ramazan Temirov.
articles.body: Lone’er Kavanagh has not made major changes to his preparation for Ramazan Temirov. The British flyweight says the work has centred on mistakes from his last fight, a submission loss to Brandon Royval in July.“There hasn't been too much change. It's more about learning from the mistakes I made in the last fight,” Kavanagh told TimesofIndia.com ahead of his UFC 333 fight on October 24 at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. “I have such a good team around me that we're always evolving and working on the finer details - the little things we need to improve.”Kavanagh, ranked sixth in the UFC flyweight division, faces 10th-ranked Temirov. The fight comes after a year in which he beat former champion Brandon Moreno by unanimous decision in February before losing to Royval in July. Both bouts went beyond the opening round, but ended differently for the 27-year-old.“Both fights have taught me a lot, and I'm going to continue learning from them,” Kavanagh said. “Every fight I have and every mistake I make will teach me something until the day I retire. I think that's the main thing - I'm always learning.”The Moreno fight was a five-round test against a former champion, while Royval submitted Kavanagh with a rear-naked choke in the third round. The latter bout also earned both fighters Fight of the Night honours. Kavanagh now returns to the Octagon against an opponent coming off a first-round knockout.Temirov stopped former flyweight title challenger Steve Erceg in July, extending his winning streak to 12 fights. The Uzbek fighter has a 20-3 professional record, including 12 knockout wins and 11 first-round finishes.“Obviously, Ramazan is very powerful. He likes to come forward and land big shots, and I feel like that works very well for me,” Kavanagh said. “As long as I stay focused and switched on, I'm able to make it a good fight and keep myself safe.”Temirov called out Kavanagh after the Erceg victory. The Englishman, however, sees little reason to read a personal motive into the challenge.“I think it's just a fight that makes sense, right? Obviously, he wants to climb up the rankings, and I was next on the ladder,” Kavanagh said. “So I don't take it personally because I do the same thing. I'm always looking to climb upwards.”The rankings give the bout a clear purpose. Kavanagh is looking to consolidate his position after the Royval defeat, while Temirov has the chance to beat a top-six opponent after his win over Erceg. For Kavanagh, the immediate target is to establish himself as a future title contender.“I think it's a good fight to establish myself as a future title contender,” he said. “He's got a good record and is coming off a good win, so I feel like the winner will be right back at the top.”He is not ready to name a preferred opponent beyond Saturday. Kavanagh said he would speak to his coach and manager after the fight before deciding on his next move.“I'm not too sure yet. I'm very much a one-fight-at-a-time kind of person,” he said. “So, I'll get this one done first, then we'll speak to my coach and my manager and see what's next.”Asked what version of himself fans should expect to see against Temirov, Kavanagh returned to the idea of continued improvement.“The best version of myself - the one that's always improving,” he said. “And, yeah, that's what's going to happen.”UFC 333 will be live on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Smith vs Puello: Tony Bellew says world champion should target Adam Azim at Hillsborough
articles.summary: In his BBC Sport column, Tony Bellew explains why Dalton Smith could be British boxing's next superstar - and why he should fight Adam Azim at Hillsborough.
articles.body:
Briton Dalton Smith defends his WBC light-welterweight title against Dominican Republic's Alberto Puello on Saturday after stunning Subriel Matias in January . Former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew explains why an Adam Azim fight at Hillsborough could make Smith a household name.

Dalton Smith has everything it takes to become British boxing's next superstar.

He's one of the best fighters in this country, pound-for-pound, and I'd even go as far as saying he's a better boxer than I ever was.

But there's a difference between being a brilliant fighter and becoming a household name. I know that from my own career.

My old mate David Haye was the fighter who took my popularity to another level entirely. The whole country thought I was going to get knocked out, but the British public love an underdog story and when I woke up the morning after beating Haye for the first time, my profile had exploded.

Suddenly, grandmothers were stopping me in the street telling me they wanted me to punch his head in. Everybody had an opinion.

Dalton needs his own Haye - that rival who takes him from being known among boxing fans to being recognised by the whole country.

It's a rivalry which has been brewing for years and I'd love to see them fight at Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough Stadium. It would be a monster fight.

But before any of that, Dalton has a massive job to do against Alberto Puello on Saturday. A defeat would be a massive blow for British boxing because this kid is one of the brightest lights we've got.

I've known about Dalton since his days on the Great Britain amateur squad. I was surprised he didn't stay amateur for the Olympics because I fancied him to win a medal. But look at him now.

Dalton isn't somebody who says outrageous things like Tyson Fury or creates controversy like Derek Chisora. He does his talking in the ring and I respect that.

He showed us just how good he was by dethroning the much-feared Matias in New York. I told Eddie Hearn on the morning of the fight that Dalton would stop him. Eddie couldn't believe it, but I was absolutely convinced.

It was a phenomenal performance, but what makes Dalton so special is his timing.

He reminds me of another brilliant Sheffield fighter, Kell Brook. He's not necessarily the strongest, quickest or sharpest, but technically he does everything really well. He catches opponents in the middle of exchanges with perfect timing.

I admire his relationship with his father and trainer, Grant, who has allowed Dalton to travel and learn from different trainers.

I've had coaches who wouldn't entertain bringing somebody else in to help. Grant understands that no trainer knows everything and Dalton has benefited enormously from that.

People are overlooking Puello, which is dangerous. Even though Matias beat him, I genuinely believe this is the toughest fight of Dalton's career.

He's a southpaw with a phenomenal work rate and a granite chin. I've hardly ever seen him badly hurt.

But Puello is easier to hit than most southpaws because he doesn't use his stance particularly well. I wish I'd faced a few like that during my career – unfortunately, I had to deal with some southpaw guy called Oleksandr Usyk.

My only slight concern for Dalton is his work rate. He can't afford to start slowly or he could find himself four or five rounds behind.

He must approach every round as a new fight. Don't go looking for the knockout. Go in there looking to win eight, nine or 10 rounds.

If he stops Puello, I'll regard him as clearly the best fighter in the division. Even beating him on points would be a brilliant achievement.

Afterwards, I don't want to see him jumping through weight divisions chasing big names.

Marvin Hagler showed you can become a legend by dominating one division. Stay at light-welterweight, unify the belts and make everybody come to you.

Dalton has already achieved his dream of becoming world champion. Nobody can ever take that WBC green-and-gold belt away from him.

I know he dreams of fighting at Hillsborough and I understand exactly what that means. Winning the WBC title at Goodison Park, the former home of my beloved Everton, was my lifelong dream, which I achieved by knocking out Ilunga Makabu in 2016.

Dalton needs the right opponent for his own special night and to make him into a mainstream star.

There are huge names out there and Dalton is capable of competing with the very best. But for me, Azim would be the one.

There is nothing quite like a domestic rivalry and the atmosphere would be incredible. Two top British fighters, a genuine rivalry and promoters Hearn and Ben Shalom going at each other in the build-up.

Azim is lightning fast, possibly the quickest fighter in British boxing pound-for-pound. But timing beats speed, and that's what makes this rivalry so fascinating.

I'd love Azim to win a world title first, then they could meet in a unification fight. It could even become a trilogy.

But beating Puello is no formality and Dalton cannot afford to lose focus. Then we can start dreaming about Azim and Hillsborough.

Tony Bellew was speaking to BBC Sport boxing journalist Kal Sajad.

articles.body:
Take everything you think you know about amateur wrestling and mix in Hulk Hogan's lingering aura.

There you have the artist known as Real American Freestyle, a Tampa-based outfit billing itself as the "first unscripted pro wrestling league for the best athletes in the world."

Founded in April 2025 by Hogan, former WCW executive Eric Bischoff, Chad Bronstein and Izzy Martinez, the organization has produced numbered events since August 2025. Its latest, RAF 14—live from the Fontainebleau Las Vegas and headlined by a middleweight crossover title bout between Arman Tsarukyan and Dillon Danis—will air live on Fox Nation.

Hogan, 71, died 37 days before the organization's inaugural event.

The "crossover" divisions are for athletes known primarily for their work outside of freestyle wrestling, and Friday's show will include Tsarukyan and Danis, Khamzat Chimaev and Robbie Lawler, Pat Downey and Magomed Magomedkerimov, and Brendan Allen and Alexander Shlemenko in four crossover bouts.

articles.title: WOW 33 Vitoria calienta motores con en rueda de prensa: "Las MMA me cambiaron la vida"
articles.standfirst: Este jueves el Buesa Arena fue testigo de las últimas declaraciones de los ocho protagonistas principales de la cartelera
articles.summary: Este jueves el Buesa Arena fue testigo de las últimas declaraciones de los ocho protagonistas principales de la cartelera
articles.body: Dos días quedan para que el Buesa Arena de Vitoria albergue WOW 33. Este sábado 24 de octubre, la promotora líder de las MMA nacionales regresa al País Vasco con un evento lleno de acción, y este jueves se ha celebrado la rueda de prensa oficial de la que han formado parte los cuatro combates principales de la cartelera. Jonny Becerra, Kaique Modesto, Daniel Richardson, Willmar Quirama, Arkaitz 'Gudari' Ramos, Jeferson Costa, Ander Sánchez y Borja García han dicho sus últimas palabras antes del gran día, donde se espera una olla a presión. Unos de los primeros en hablar han sido Daniel Richardson y Willmar Quirama, que han prometido acción al ser dos prospectos invictos con muchas expectativas puestos sobre ellos. "Al entrar a la jaula no temo a nada, es uno de los pocos momentos en mi vida en los que me siento vivo", dijo el peleador del Climent Club, mientras que Quirama afirmó que "dentro de la jaula nos matamos, pero no dejamos de ser personas. Las artes marciales me cambiaron la vida. Antes era una persona agresiva y después cambié". Sin duda, otro de los nombres propios de la rueda de prensa fue Jonny Becerra, que destacó lo mucho que repudia la violencia fuera de la jaula la venir de un barrio conflictivo y aprender lo que estaba mal a base de golpes. Además, en esta ocasión buscará redimirse de sus derrota en el WOW Bilbao de hace unos meses, algo de lo que aprendió mucho. "Descubrí que la resiliencia no es solo una palabra, es algo que se siente", sentenció. Más tarde fue Arkaitz 'Gudari' el que respondió a las preguntas de la prensa, con MARCA allí presente, y dejó claro que no le supone ninguna presión añadida ser uno de los ídolos locales. "Para mí no hay ningún tipo de presión, para mí esto es un regalo al final de mi carrera y tener toda esa gente que me apoya, pues es algo increíble e impensable cuando empecé en este deporte", reveló. Más tarde fue el turno del combate estelar entre Borja García y Ander Sánchez, dos de los nombres más mediáticos del panorama nacional. "Si pienso que me va a ganar, mejor no vengo. Pienso que lo voy a pasar por encima y es lo que va a pasar. No estoy hablando de prepotente, pero es lo que pienso. Al fin y al cabo esto es mi vida y es un paso más hacia donde quiero llegar, que es muy difícil", afirmaba 'El Águila'. Ander, por su parte, entiende los juegos mentales de su rival. "Creo que no hay ninguna guerra. Él dice lo que tiene que decir. Es un rival que está preparado y que se lo cree. Yo entiendo que él tiene que decirlo, pero simplemente yo vengo aquí a luchar, ya digo bastantes cosas en mis vídeos que no tienen que ver con las peleas y simplemente pues en la jaula saldré a decir lo que tengo que decir y a mostrar cómo me he preparado", finalizó.

articles.title: Tsarukyan insiste en que será el próximo en pelear por el título... ¿contra Topuria?
articles.standfirst: El peleador armenio cree que Gaethje se retirará y se medirá a otro contendiente del peso ligero
articles.summary: El peleador armenio cree que Gaethje se retirará y se medirá a otro contendiente del peso ligero
articles.body: Arman Tsarukyan ha vuelto a hablar, y ha dejado claro que será el siguiente contendiente al título de peso ligero. Tras noquear a Mauricio Ruffy en el primer asalto en el UFC 331, el peleador armenio ha confesado que la compañía le tiene en cuenta para el siguiente combate por el cinturón, aunque ha dejado caer que posiblemente su rival no sea Justin Gaethje, actual campeón, ya que podría retirarse para dejar paso a otros nombres como Ilia Topuria o Paddy Pimblett. Gaethje ya afirmó hace unas semanas que todavía no había tomado una decisión respecto a su futuro, por lo que de momento su decisión es una incógnita. Sin embargo, teniendo en cuenta que ya ha cumplido todos los objetivos de su carrera tras finalizar a Ilia Topuria en el UFC Casa Blanca y convertirse en campeón indiscutido, lo más normal es que decida poner fin a una de las trayectorias más impresionantes que se recuerdan en la UFC. Tsarukyan apunta a una pelea por el cinturón a principios de 2027, y así lo ha hecho saber en una entrevista con MMA Fighting. "Por lo que he oído, mi próximo combate será por el título. A principios del año que viene, más o menos", sentenció. Hace unas horas, Arman fue más allá en otra entrevista con Ariel Helwani, afirmando que "ya me dijeron la fecha en la que podría ser, aunque no puedo decirla. Será en el primer trimestre de 2027 en América. Me han dado dos nombres, porque creo que Gaethje se va a retirar. Si la UFC le paga mucho dinero peleará, pero no sé si la UFC le va a pagar ese dinero. El otro nombre puede ser Topuria o Pimblett. Ellos me dijeron que la revancha entre Justin e Ilia no va a suceder. Gaethje ya fue a la Casa Blanca, venció al mejor peso ligero... ¿Por qué iba a aceptar una pelea con Arman Tsarukyan". Teniendo en cuenta que en enero el evento numerado será en Toronto -Canadá-, las otras dos fechas que quedan son en febrero o marzo, por lo que será ahí cuando compita por el cinturón. Lo que falta por saber es ese rival del que habla en caso de que Justin se retire, ya que Topuria es la mayor superestrella de la división y Paddy de someter a Benoit Saint-Denis en el primer asalto. Si sus declaraciones son ciertas, la primera gran noticia es que 'El Matador' no podrá vengarse de su única derrota profesional ante Gaethje, y la segunda que quizás su regreso vuelva a ser por el título indiscutido. De momento no hay nada oficial, pero se espera que en los próximos meses la situación se aclare y todas las piezas del puzzle vayan encajando.

articles.title: UFC 333: Merab Dvalishvili gains 19lb in five hours before world title fight
articles.summary: Merab Dvalishvili says he has gained 19lb (1st 5lb) in just five hours after weighing in for his bantamweight title fight against Petr Yan at UFC 333 on Saturday.
articles.body:
Merab Dvalishvili says he has gained 19lb (1st 5lb) in just five hours after weighing in for his bantamweight title fight against Petr Yan at UFC 333 on Saturday.

The Georgian weighed 135lb (9st 9lb), which was the same as Russian champion Yan, before the pair's co-main event fight in Abu Dhabi.

Dvalishvili later uploaded a video to Instagram showing the 35-year-old stepping on scales and weighing 154lb (11st 0lb).

"I've been drinking water and in only five hours I gain back 19 pounds, that's what we do, let's go," he said.

"Now I'm back drinking and recovering. Now I'm going to start eating. Eat food first, then tomorrow you guys already know who I'm going to eat."

Fighters typically cut weight by shedding water in the days before a bout, before rehydrating to regain weight - a process that can provide a physical advantage inside the octagon.

The UFC has taken a number of steps to make weight cuts safer over the years, including banning IV drips, which forces fighters to hydrate in a healthier way, and building the Performance Institute, which provides guidance for its athletes from professional health experts.

UFC fighters are recommended to lose no more than 8% of their body weight during fight week.

On fight night they are recommended to stay within 10% of their weight class.

Dvalishvili is aiming to win back the title he lost against two-time champion Yan last December.

During their face-off, the pair engaged in an intense but respectful stare-down.

In the main event, champion Alexander Volkanovski and Movsar Evloev both made weight before their featherweight world title contest.

Australia's Volkanovski is looking to earn a record ninth win in UFC featherweight title fights against Russia's Evloev, who is undefeated in 20 bouts.

On the undercard, British flyweight Lone'er Kavanagh takes on Uzbekistan's Ramazan Temirov.

The 27-year-old Kavanagh is aiming to bounce back from defeat by American Brandon Royval in July.

articles.title: Joaquin Buckley Reveals MMA Retirement Timeline After KO Loss, Talks Grandmother's Impact in Video
articles.summary: UFC fighter Joaquin Buckley announced Thursday night that he is retiring from MMA after his next fight.
articles.body:
UFC fighter Joaquin Buckley announced Thursday night that he is retiring from MMA after his next fight.

In a video posted by Happy Punch on X, Buckley noted that the result of his most recent fight and the manner in which it impacted his family led to his decision:

"Hearing my grandmother speak and listening to her talk, and hearing her cry about me having to stop doing this sport because she couldn't believe what she saw, ya'll don't know how that affected me," Buckley said.

Buckley admitted that it was a "hard" decision, but since he is "so far away" from his goal of becoming world champion, it "doesn't make any sense" to continue fighting.

His most recent bout saw him fall to Mike Malott at UFC Fight Night last weekend via second-round knockout.

Malott caught Buckley flush on the chin with a knee, causing Buckley to go limp and fall to the canvas. Malott went in for the finish, but the referee quickly stepped in and ended the fight:

For Buckley, it was his third consecutive loss, bringing his career record to 21-9 with 15 wins by way of knockout.

The 32-year-old fighter from St. Louis turned pro in 2014, and he made his UFC debut in 2020 in a loss to Kevin Holland.

From May 2023 to December 2024, Buckley reeled off six consecutive wins in the welterweight division, including arguably the biggest victory of his career when he beat former UFC welterweight champion Colby Covington.

Buckley was seemingly closing in on a title shot of his own at that point, but a unanimous-decision loss to Kamaru Usman last year, followed by losses to Sean Brady and Malott halted his progress.

Given his recent struggles, Buckley is ready to step away from the sport of MMA, but he is committed to having one more fight before doing so.

articles.title: Joe Cordina says he's been offered Manny Pacquiao fight as part of Anthony Joshua-Tyson Fury bill in Cardiff
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set for December 11 showdown at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, hometown boy Joe Cordina tells Sky Sports he has agreed to fight 47-year-old boxing icon Manny Pacquiao on the undercard but that contracts haven't yet been signed
articles.body:
The 34-year-old has confirmed that he has agreed to fight the boxing icon at the Principality Stadium in his birth city of Cardiff, but that no contracts have been signed as of yet.

Sky Sports have approached Pacquiao's team for comment.

"I've been offered the fight," said Cordina, a two-time super-featherweight world champion. "They asked me if I'd fight Pacquiao: this is what the deal is, otherwise they're going to offer it to someone else.

"'Of course', I said, 'No problem'. I've won world titles, and don't get me wrong, I want to win more. But, for me, the name of Manny Pacquiao at this present moment is bigger than any name in boxing.

"He's an eight-division world champion, a legend. But a global superstar like him will be gone in the next year or so.

"So for me to be able to share the ring with someone who I grew up watching before I even started boxing, it would be an honour."

Cordina added: "Don't get me wrong, it's nowhere near done. I haven't been sent a contract, I haven't been sent anything and I haven't been told yet it's happening.

"I've been offered it, I've said yes, agreed everything and I'm now just waiting for them to either tell me yes or no?

"I'm training as if I am fighting Manny Pacquiao. I've been training for the last four or five weeks.

In terms of the prospect of facing the 47-year-old Pacquiao a decade or so on from his prime, Cordina pointed to the Filipino's most recent fight against Mario Barrios in July of 2025 that ended in a draw.

"They had a draw but, to be honest, I thought he [Pacquiao] nicked it," Cordina said of the WBC welterweight title clash.

"I've seen loads of people be like, 'Why are you fighting Manny Pacquiao? He's an old man'.

"But the last thing to go is power. You see him on the bags and he's still got speed, he's still sharp and his footwork is still there. Yes, his timing might be off - he hasn't been in the ring for a year and a half - and that might be the thing that is his undoing.

"But he's had so many fights; he's an eight-division world champion, he knows his way around the ring, he's not a novice. He's been around the block; he's boxed everybody."

As for potentially being on the same bill as Joshua and Fury, Cordina hopes the long-anticipated fight lives up to the billing, while he also doesn't buy Joshua as an underdog.

"You can never write off a heavyweight anyway, but especially when it's Anthony Joshua," Cordina said.

"It only takes one shot from him, and you're in Barney Rubble [trouble].

"They're both going to go out there and go straight at it; they're going to meet in the middle of the ring and just have a crack.

"Whether it goes down like that or not, I don't know, but that's what I'd like to happen, to see them have a shootout like in a Western.

"It'd be an anti-climax otherwise. This fight has been talked about for years - and it's probably come five years too late.

"I just believe that can't be a bore fest. They've got to go out there and go at it."

articles.title: La hora de Alexander Volkanovski, el GOAT más querido de la UFC
articles.standfirst: El peleador australiano, uno de los campeones más emblemáticos que han pasado por la compañía, pondrá en juego el cinturón de peso pluma este sábado ante Movsar Evloev en el UFC 333
articles.summary: El peleador australiano, uno de los campeones más emblemáticos que han pasado por la compañía, pondrá en juego el cinturón de peso pluma este sábado ante Movsar Evloev en el UFC 333
articles.body: Este sábado 24 de octubre llegó la hora de Alexander Volkanovski (28-4). El GOAT de peso pluma vuelve al octágono para poner en juego su cinturón de peso pluma ante Movsar Evloev (20-0) en combate estelar del UFC 333 de Abu Dhabi, con el objetivo de agrandar su legado y dejar sus últimas pinceladas a una carrera envidiable y a una personalidad única que le han convertido en uno de los peleadores más queridos de la historia. Porque sí, es cierto que hay varios GOATs en la UFC en diferentes categorías, pero pocos o ninguno han conseguido calar tanto en la gente como 'The Great'. Ni Jon Jones, ni Anderson Silva, ni Khabib Nurmagomedov, ni Georges St-Pierre han conseguido que el público vaya en su favor al unísono. Siempre ha habido algún hater o algún sector de los fanáticos que no coincidian a la hora de catalogar a estos nombres, pero con 'Volk' todo es diferente. Tras un periplo por el rugby dio el salto a las MMA, y lo cierto es que el camino a su primer reinado en el peso pluma no fue ni mucho menos agradable. Tras barrer con la división, le tocó medirse a Max Holloway, lo que es sinónimo de adoptar el papel de villano por lo carismático que es 'Blessed'. Después de una pelea muy ajustada fue el australiano el que se coronó como nuevo campeón, y en la revancha se llevó la victoria por decisión dividida cuando muchos le vieron perder. Teniendo en cuenta quién es Holloway, esta decisión provocó una oleada de hate hacia Volkanovski, que sin querer se convirtió en enemigo público número uno. Sin embargo, solo le hizo falta ser él mismo para revertir la situación. Acto seguido venció a Brian Ortega después de sobrevivir de manera increíble a dos intentos de sumisión, noqueó a 'The Korean Zombie' y llegó el momento de cerrar la trilogía con Holloway, dándole una paliza y demostrando de una vez por todas que estaba destinado a ser el 'GOAT' de la categoría. Esto le permitió ser el número 1 en el ránking libra por libra, y curiosamente fue su primera derrota en la UFC la que le hizo ser más querido que nunca. Islam Makhachev le abrió las puertas a subir a peso ligero para intentar ser doble campeón, y a pesar de perder por decisión unánime le demostró al mundo de qué pasta estaba hecho. Es más, ni siquiera esta victoria del daguestaní le permitió arrebatar a 'Volk' el trono del ránking libra por libra. Tras finalizar a Yair Rodríguez y defender de nuevo el cinturón en peso pluma, una lesión de Charles Oliveira poco antes de enfrentarse a Makhachev llevó a la UFC a ofrecerle una revancha en corto aviso. Un error fatal que acabó con Volkanovski noqueado en el primer asalto y reconociendo que había aceptado la pelea porque necesitaba subirse al octágono para evitar que le dominasen los demonios internos con los que estaba conviviendo. De nuevo la gente se volcó con él a pesar de caer derrotado, incluso el propio Makhachev, ya que pocas veces un campeón de su calibre es capaz de abrirse de esta manera con la gente. Y 'Volk' no mentía, ya que a pesar de caer noqueado decidió volver a los cuatro meses para defender su cinturón de peso pluma ante Ilia Topuria, volviendo a perder por K.O. y hundiéndose aún más en su propio pozo. Esta vez el australiano sí que decidió tomarse más de un año de descanso, y para entender la magnitud de su persona hasta el propio Topuria afirmó que no quería volver a enfrentarse a él porque le caía demasiado bien. Ni sus rivales, ni el público, ni nadie tenía una mala palabra hacia 'The Great'. Por ese mismo motivo, cuando 'El Matador' subió a peso ligero y dejó vacante el cinturón en las 145 libras, todo el mundo quería que Alexander recuperase el trono, algo que logró en abril de 2025 al superar por decisión unánime a Diego Lopes. Por si fuera poco, el pasado febrero logró volver a vencer al brasileño con otra gran actuación, y este sábado se enfrentará a un prospecto invicto con la intención de demostrar que sigue vigente. Si ya es difícil de por sí enfrentar a alguien del talento de Volkanovski, tiene que serlo mucho más cuando sus rivales se dan cuenta de que no hay motivos más allá de los deportivos para querer vencer a esa persona. Sin crearse un personaje ni buscar beef con nadie, el australiano se ha ganado el corazón de todo el mundo, y eso es mucho más preciado que cualquier cinturón que haya podido ganar a lo largo de su carrera.

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan the influencer draws far more attention than Arman Tsarukyan the fighter
articles.summary: We didn't actually think his RAF 14 wrestling match with Dillon Danis would go without incident, did we?
articles.body:
If I had to give a percentage, I'd say that Arman Tsarukyan is 77% influencer at this point, and 23% fighter. If he were a bigger gambler, it would be fitting to see him sitting next to Dana White at a Vegas baccarat table, maybe alongside other luminaries such as Adin Ross and SteveWillDoit, throwing around six-figure bets to make Instagram reels.

As it stands, he prefers to punch people. Or to tackle them off a raised platform. Or to head-butt them. It just depends on the mood (and the battery life of his camera guy). So long as it's out of competition — or in the very least, out of bounds — "everything is content."

Knowing that, we didn't actually think that his wrestling match with Dillon Danis, combat sport's tawdriest of provocateurs, would go without incident, did we? At Thursday's RAF 14 press conference, all it took was for Danis to stand up and show off his T-shirt for Tsarukyan to come flying off the rails .

"It says Khamzat's my b****," Danis boasted. "And it has a picture with him without a beard." Danis, it should be noted, lasted just 44 seconds against Chimaev at RAF 10 in June, which perhaps makes the shirt ironical.

Next thing he knew, though, Tsarukyan — who is Khamzat's friend and training partner — was on his side of the dais, throwing punches through a small republic of RAF security men, hoping that one might slip through and clip his chin. A miniature-scale pandemonium occurred, perhaps a solid five on a scale of zero-to-Khabib Nurmagomedov-talon-swooping-Danis-off-the-Octagon at UFC 229.

Impulses, especially when unchecked, make for perfect content, and that content went immediately viral. The clip went out everywhere, which is the perfect build for tonight's RAF 14 main event in Las Vegas. It's doubtful Danis will have an answer for Tsarukyan on the mats (he never really does), but there is a good chance that further incidents will ensue. In fact, it feels like a near guarantee.

This is the Tsarukyan experience; it has less to do with competition, and more to do with what happens around it.

This is why Dana White has a special doghouse for Tsarukyan, because of his brattishness, his sense of privilege and his general insubordinate attitude. For those same reasons, RAF loves him. In fact, you wonder if RAF stands for Real Arman Fanatics, the way they give him free rein.

RAF, the wrestling league in which Tsarukyan has competed eight times already, loves when Arman gets to acting up. The moment people started paying real attention to RAF was the moment Tsarukyan shoved and punched Georgio Poullas at RAF 6 after the bell, a sequence that can only be considered "extracurricular." Yet it went viral, too. The MMA websites did some heavy traffic that weekend, and the rematch was made like 15 minutes later .

Yet as UFC 333 gets set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Saturday , it's Arman who steals the Friday spotlight. Because he is the No. 1 contender at lightweight, there's a scaffolding in place to care about his doings. And there's a double-down element to Tsarukyan punching away at Danis because of an offending T-shirt. He was on his best behavior against Mauricio Ruffy in punching his ticket as the next challenger for Justin Gaethje at UFC 331 last month, a changed man, but this latest thing is what they call "recidivism" in Clark County courtrooms.

He is who he is and will be so long as social media exists. This is the shtick that works for him, and you can only hope that Dana — who runs a reprehensible sport called PowerSlap for his share in the click game — sees the ambitions in play. Being in business with a loose cannon isn't all that bad when the idea is to direct attention at what you're doing.

It wasn't that long ago that Arman punched some dude on his way to punch Charles Oliveira at UFC 300. He just coolly unloaded on some smart-mouth fan on his walkout, the way other fighters might high-five someone. Nothing much came of it in terms of punishment, yet it was the first sign of Tsarukyan's brand of unruliness.

It feels like it's been a million things since. Take your pick … him being kicked off an American Airlines flight from Los Angeles to Philadelphia for refusing to follow safety regulations … him tackling Urijah Faber off the RAF raised platform once he was there two days later … him head-butting Dan Hooker during a faceoff in Qatar, which ultimately cost him the title shot he was promised … the brawl at RAF 6 after Poullas … all that stuff with Nina Drama … and now this.

Dillon Danis , who incites brawls just by walking into a room in cartoon sneakers. Danis, who is banned from UFC events. He is the cheap thrill of the fight game. If Danis were a liquor, he'd be hooch. He'd be Mad Dog 20/20. He'd come in a paper bag. Dillon Danis, who knows he can expect meatheaded responses because he is the valedictorian of meatheads, and yet he played Tsarukyan like a puppet.

Or Tsarukyan played him. Nobody's really counting, unless we're speaking specifically in clicks.

articles.title: Report: Wrestling legend Ric Flair collapses after complaining of blood clots
articles.summary: Professional wrestling star Ric Flair was hospitalized in Florida Friday after falling down outside a Tampa restaurant. The 77-year-old grappler nicknamed “t...
articles.body:
Professional wrestling star Ric Flair was hospitalized in Florida Friday after falling down outside a Tampa restaurant.

The 77-year-old grappler nicknamed "the Nature Boy" fell and injured his face after leaving to walk across a street, according to TMZ.

He'd left his phone and drink on the bar. Medical personnel rushed to help Flair, who was reportedly bleeding heavily from one eye and possibly concussed. He was said to have been taken to an area hospital by ambulance.

Flair had earlier posted a message to fans in Washington apologizing for being unable to attend a Friday event in Seattle due to blood clots.

"Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3-4 hours," he wrote on Facebook.

Flying to Seattle, he said, would be outside that time frame. Flair said he's scheduled to undergo a procedure on the affected vein that will remedy the situation.

"As disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first," he added.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was sidelined for the remainder of the NFL season this week after doctors discovered he had a blood clot in one of his legs that could've killed him had it traveled to his lungs. Flair mentioned that in his post in which he warned that blood clots can be life-threatening and must not be taken lightly.

Flair's representatives haven't responded to a request for comment.

articles.title: UFC 333 predictions
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski faces the undefeated Movsar Evloev, and Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili face off one more time
articles.body:
One way or another, history will be made at UFC 333. Maybe more than once.

First, you have Alexander Volkanovski, facing the classic combat sports conundrum of getting older while the competitions only gets younger and hungrier. "The Great" has done it all in his career and has nothing left to prove—other than maybe that he belongs to be placed even higher on the all-time great list than he already is.

He couldn't ask for a more compelling challenge than Movsar Evloev. The undefeated Evloev has battled inactivity and a lack of fan-friendly highlights to earn his shot, going 10-0 in the UFC and bumping every other contender out of his way. Inside the distance or on the cards, winning's winning , as a wise man once said.

Then there's Petr Yan, once hanging on to the edge of the title picture by a thread, now back where he belongs in the greatest bantamweight of all time discussion. All he had to do was defeat three ranked opponents and then deliver the performance of his life this past December to avenge a past loss and become champion a second time.

The man he beat, Merab Dvalishvili, can restore order and cement himself as the 135-pound GOAT if he wins his series with Yan. Dvalishvili might have flown too close to the sun in 2025, attempting to become the first UFC fighter to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year; now, with 10 months to rest, recover, and evolve, can he get back to his overwhelming ways and go on another dominant run?

Elsewhere on a stacked main card, Lone'er Kavanagh and Ramazan Temirov jockey for position in an increasingly crowded flyweight division, Alexander Volkov looks to keep his heavyweight title hopes alive when he takes on Rizvan Kuniev, and Aaron Pico faces short-notice replacement Losene Keita in a sizzling featherweight opener.

When: Saturday, Oct. 24. The five-fight early preliminary card begins at 10 a.m. ET, followed by a four-fight preliminary card at 12 p.m. ET. The five-fight main card begins at 2 p.m. ET with the entire event streaming live on Paramount+.

(Numbers in parentheses indicate standing in the MMA Fighting Global Rankings and Pound-for-Pound Rankings )

Alexander Volkanovski (1, P4P-5) vs. Movsar Evloev (2, P4P-19)

For the first time in a while, I can say with confidence that Alexander Volkanovski's time is up.

All credit to Volkanovski for silencing the doubters time and time again, and for never wavering from wanting to give Movsar Evloev an opportunity. It's hardly an unwinnable fight for the venerated Volkanovski, as his all-around game remains as sharp as ever, plus he's survived the wrestling of Islam Makhachev and lived to tell about it. Keep it on the feet, box Evloev up, and live to fight another day as champion.

Making the case for Evloev, I want to shut down the notion that his lack of finishes somehow makes him less of a championship threat. Look at his most recent wins: Lerone Murphy, Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen, Diego Lopes, Dan Ige, heck, throw Hakeem Dawodu in there. Which of those fighters is easy to finish? Those are some of the toughest outs at 145 pounds, so yes, while we'd love to have seen Evloev put a stamp on his No. 1 contender status by emphatically putting one of those names away, it's not essential.

As far as Evloev's skills go, obviously his clearest path to victory involves grounding Volkanovski, smothering him against the fence, just wearing the older fighter down for 25 minutes. That said, and I could be fooling myself, I think Evloev actually finds his first finish here. Volkanovski gets hit. Lopes caught him. Makhachev and Ilia Topuria knocked him out. When Evloev throws, he has some pop to his punches, and all it takes is one good one to rattle Volkanovski's chin these days.

So yes, I'm counting out Volkanovski. Again. And I'm ready to look dumb. Again. Give me a fresh face at the top, though, and Volkanovski moving one step closer to a well-deserved retirement.

Petr Yan (1, P4P-2) vs. Merab Dvalishvili (2, P4P-10)

I hate to take away from Petr Yan's amazing performance in their rematch, but did we really see the best version of Merab Dvalishvili that night?

Look, I'm a man of science—and Xyience, obviously—and I can say with 90 percent confidence that cutting weight and preparing for four title fights in 12 months can't possibly be good for you, even if you have Dvalishvili's freakish physical and mental conditioning. Then you remember the fourth was against Yan, a guy who might just be the best ever at 135 pounds who already had three rounds of data to work with. Trouble.

Yan denied Dvalishvili at every turn in their second fight, never letting Dvalishvili reach that extra gear that has broken so many challengers. Unsurprisingly, Yan got the better of the majority of the striking exchanges, showing once again that he is pound-for-pound one of the best strikers in all of MMA. I don't see a scenario where Dvalishvili wins on the feet, even as much as his standup skills have improved.

Where Dvalishvili excels is in relentlessly mixing up his techniques and, yes, frustrating his opponents with his wrestling whether it's against the fence or on the ground. His main goal is to give his opponents zero room to breathe, much less think. That's how he beat Yan the first time and it's a strategy that is repeatable, albeit with a few tweaks.

At their very best, I lean slightly towards Dvalishvili, but not for a second do I think either fighter will have a comfortable lead on the cards this time around. We could even take a trip to Splitty City. I hope not, but I do suspect we'll be treated to a close decision—one that possibly sets up a fourth encounter down the road.

Lone'er Kavanagh (8) vs. Ramazan Temirov (12)

The 27-year-old Kavanagh has been swimming with the sharks since his third UFC fight, when he received a rude awakening from Mr. Spoiler himself, Charles Johnson. He followed that up with a career-best performance against two-time flyweight champion Brandon Moreno and then had to tap out in the third round of a gritty battle with another elite veteran, Brandon Royval. Ramazan Temirov is closer to Kavanagh in terms of octagon experience, but arguably just as dangerous as those other standouts.

Outside of Manel Kape, Temirov might be the scariest hitter at 125 pounds. He's blessed with one-shot knockout power and he'll be looking land a hammer before Kavanagh can establish any sort of rhythm. I believe Kavanagh has learned a ton from his past three fights though, even if it's only that there are levels to this. Now it's his turn to impart a version of that lesson on Temirov.

Watch for Kavanagh to stick and move for three rounds, mix the martial arts, and outlast Temirov en route to another impressive decision win.

Alexander Volkov (4) vs. Rizvan Kuniev (9)

I'll be honest, I didn't have Alexander Volkov becoming The People's Champ on my bingo card. But here we are, as much of the community has rallied around Volkov being robbed of a heavyweight title shot after years of battling top 10 opponents.

Rizvan Kuniev is the scariest kind of up-and-coming heavyweight in that he actually does stuff . That might sound like the faintest of praise, but in this division, being busy and pushing the pace immediately separates you from the pack. Ciryl Gane, Josh Hokit, and Gable Steveson are the names that spring to the mind of most fans when talking about athletic heavys, but I feel like Kuniev is flying under the radar in these discussions. He's always coming forward and looking to engage and he has the cardio to drown Volkov with volume for 15 minutes.

Maybe I just need to see more of Big Riz, but I still think Volkov has the edge in striking and grappling. He's one of the few giants we've seen in MMA that actually knows how to utilize his reach advantage (he's not amazing at it, but better than Stefan Struve, to put it nicely), and that length should keep Kuniev from just walking him down with no repercussions. Taking Kuniev down is unlikely, but should the fight go to the ground, the more experienced Volkov can give Kuniev some problems.

Full disclosure, this is as much of a hope pick as anything else, because it would be a damn shame if Volkov never received his UFC title shot. I fully expect Kuniev to be a contender for years to come, so let tonight be Volkov's night as he comes out on the right end of a hard-fought decision.

I'll say it: I don't believe in the more measured, more mature Aaron Pico. Even though he put together a fine three-round performance against Patricio Pitbull, the berserker is still in there. And Losene Keita is the kind of opponent who can bring it out.

If I'm wrong about this, then I'll be thrilled, because we need more fighters like Pico and if he's learned to consistently channel his aggression and prodigious talents into a complete approach to the game, even better. What worries me here is that he's arguably landed himself in an even more dangerous situation with Keita stepping in to replace an injured Arnold Allen, who was the perfect opponent to move Pico up the rankings and give him a few more high-level rounds. Keita is more willing to risk it all to make a statement.

Call this a coin flip, but I've seen Pico go full desperado too many times to trust him, especially against a guy who's only loss inside the distance was due to a freak leg injury. Keita strikes first, gets the knockout, and takes home another $100,000 bonus.
